newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks close higher, snapping losing streak. [CORRECTED 23:14 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks close higher, snapping losing streak. [CORRECTED 23:14 GMT]

text.p: Wall Street stocks closed higher on Monday, overcoming a series of hurdles to register their first rise in nearly a week.
The Dow industrials rose 41 points to close unofficially at 6919 (corrects from 6819), rallying sharply in late activity after struggling all session to overcome an opening slide of nearly 50 points.

The performance was the first show of strength by stocks since last Wednesday, when Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan delivered a blunt warning about interest rates -- one whose effects were still felt in the bond market on Monday.
The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury extended its upward creep, rising on the day to 6.84 percent from 6.80 percent.
Investors were also greeted with a rude surprise during the morning, when AT&T Corp revised downward its earnings outlook for fiscal 1997. AT&T fell 3-1/8 to 36-3/4.
The weak bond market, coupled with AT&T's decline, made the stock market's moderate gains appear all the more impressive, analysts said.
"You had two major negatives today and the market was still able to basically reverse course," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.

When buyers did emerge, they descended on the tech stocks that had led the market to record highs, and more recently in its a retreat. Intel Corp rose four to 145-7/8, International Business Machines Corp rose 1-1/2 to 145-1/4 and Microsoft Corp rose two to 99-1/2.
Analysts called the rebound encouraging but stopped well short of predicting an end to troubled times.

"It's going to be a while before these stocks regain their luster," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co. He said the techs were still well off their peaks after steep declines in recent weeks.

Also, analysts said Greenspan's scheduled appearance before the Banking Committee of the U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday and a key monthly employment report due on Friday would likely preclude any meaningful advance by stocks for the time being.
But with the broad market following techs higher and shrugging off the AT&T surprise, analysts said it was clear that at least one major shift had occurred on Wall Street.
"I'm not certain AT&T is viewed as a bellwether anymore," Barthel said. "Now we look to companies like Intel and Microsoft."
In individual issues, Conrail Inc surged 7-1/8 to 111-5/8 as expectations mounted that a four-month takeover battle for control of the railroad was nearing its conclusion.
Conrail said its board was meeting Monday to discuss the company's options. Analysts forecast that Conrail's assets would likely be divided between rival bidders CSX Corp amd Norfolk Southern Corp.
Shares in CSX jumped 2-7/8 to 49, and Norfolk Southern rose 2-3/4 to 93-7/8.
BHC Financial Inc surged 11-7/8 to 31-7/8 after the company agreed to be acquired by Fiserv Inc.
Fiserv, which agreed to pay $33.50 per share in stock for each BHC share, climbed 3-7/8 to 36-5/8.

COR Therapeutics Inc slid 2-15/16 to 9-3/8 after a Food and Drug Administration advisory panel recommended against approving intrifiban, a derivative of rattlesnake venom that the company hoped to market for treating for certain heart conditions.
The S&P 500 index rose 4.49 points to 795.31.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.18 points 1311.18.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
